title: AWS Step Functions as AI Agent Tools (Bedrock AgentCore Gateway)
content:
Your AI agent should NOT improvise a refund.
AWS just made that much easier for businesses.

On 2 November 2026, the AWS Weekly Roundup
said Step Functions workflows
are now available as AI agent tools
through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
over MCP.
The agent decides WHEN to run the workflow
and what INPUT to pass.
Step Functions then runs the steps EXACTLY
as you DEFINED THEM.
Order is not improvised by the model.

Take a refund.
Eligibility check. Then MANAGER APPROVAL.
Then credit.
That sequence stays fixed.
The model can start the tool and fill inputs,
but it cannot skip the manager step
because it feels confident.
That is the business win.

You can expose existing Standard or
Express workflows as connector targets.
Agents can also look up runs.
It is available where AgentCore Gateway is
available, at standard rates.
So if your ops team already built careful
workflows,
your agent can call them instead of
reinventing the process in prompts.

Same post also noted GPT-6.1 Terra GA on Bedrock,
the everyday-workload GPT-6 line.
OpenAI's figures say it gained about 15
points on Agents' Last Exam versus GPT-5.6
Terra,
is on par with GPT-6 Astra, and is more
than 3 times faster,
with input and output tokens at least 50
percent lower than GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-5.6
Terra,
and up to 1 million input tokens for text
and image.
Useful as cost context. Keep your focus on
the workflow tool.

Imagine you run a clinic, a shop, or an agency.
Anything IRREVERSIBLE, like a refund, a
booking cancel, or an outbound message to
a client,
belongs in a workflow tool with human approval,
not in a free-form agent chat.
Say the agent gathers the case and drafts
the action.
The Step Functions tool enforces the
order. A human still owns the risk.

Here's my take.
The companies that win with agents will
put GUARDRAILS in code and workflows,
not only in system prompts.
If a step can lose money or trust, lock the order.

Comment STEPS on Instagram and I'll DM you
the AWS blog link, or grab the link in the
LinkedIn post.
Follow for your daily AI update.
